newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Guinness recovery lifts Nigerian share trade.
newsitem.headline: Guinness recovery lifts Nigerian share trade.

text.p: Guinness Nigeria stock began a recover from a year-long slump on the Nigerian bourse on Monday and helped to lift the index by 4.69 points.
The all-share index rose to 6704.05 from 6699.36 on Friday.
Traders said the worst now seemed over for Guiness, whose fortunes, together with those of others in the sector, had been on the wane for most of the year.

"With Christmas the worst may be over for Guinness because more people tend to consume alcohol this time," said one trader, adding that Guiness's recovery was expected after shares of Nigerian Breweries began to rise on the exchange this month.
Brewers have been on hard times as economic difficulties plaguing Nigeria made most consumers kick the drinking habit.
Since January Nigerian Breweries has lost about 50 percent of its share value while Guinness fell by nearly 60 percent.
Guinness rose by 10 kobo on Monday to 5.75 naira and Nigerian Breweries by 25 kobo to 14.25 naira.
Sustained demand for West African Portland Cement saw the shares close 20 kobo higher at 39.40 naira while AIICO Insurance gained 15 kobo to 9.25 naira.
Usually active oil and food shares finished strongly. Nestle, African Petroleum and Agip eached notched 20 kobo to 43.70 naira, 38.80 naira and 18.00 naira, respectively.
Mobil was up 15 kobo at 44.75 naira, Union Dicon Salt jumped 10 kobo to 40.60 naira and Nigerian Tobacco Company ended five kobo more at 3.55 naira.
Top losers on Monday included conglomerates Lever Brothers and UAC, down 20 kobo and 10 kobo respectively at 23.40 naira and 8.90 naira.
ADC Airlines, whose jet crashed on November 7, killing more than 140 people, fell 15 kobo to 4.00 naira as some one million of its shares changed hands.
Guaranty Trust Bank fell 10 kobo to 13.00 naira and Union Bank dropped five kobo to 6.05 naira.
